cards.text: Isaiah the prophet is passing along words from the LORD, and now the LORD speaks about Assyria. It starts with "Woe to Assyria." Friend, when a message starts with woe, you do NOT want your name right after it.

cards.question: The LORD calls Assyria "the rod of My anger." What does that make Assyria?

answers.text: The tool God uses to show His anger
The nation God trusts the most
The land God promised to protect

cards.text: Then God says He'll send Assyria out on a mission. Take spoils, seize plunder and trample them down like clay in the streets.

cards.question: True or false: God sends Assyria against a nation that has been faithful to Him.

cards.text: That's the job. But the LORD says this is not Assyria's intention, this is not his plan.

cards.question: God sends Assyria on His mission, but Assyria has a plan of his own. What's in his heart?

answers.text: To destroy and cut off many nations
To do only what God sends him for
To bring the people back to God

cards.text: Then Assyria starts bragging: "Are not all my commanders kings?" Friend, I run six stations and I just go by Papa, and this guy's MIDDLE MANAGERS are kings?
Then he rattles off cities like he's reading his to-do list out loud: Calno, Carchemish, Hamath, Arpad, Samaria, Damascus.

cards.question: True or false: When Assyria lists those cities, his point is that Samaria will be harder to take than Damascus.

cards.text: He says his hand has already seized other kingdoms. Then he sizes them up next to Jerusalem and Samaria.

cards.question: What does Assyria say those kingdoms he seized had more of than Jerusalem and Samaria?
Assyria says he's already done it to Samaria and its idols. So he asks: will I not also do it to ___ and her idols?

cards.text: Now the Lord has His say. When He has completed all His work against Mount Zion and Jerusalem, He speaks about the king of Assyria, the one doing all that bragging.

cards.question: Once His work against Jerusalem is done, what will the Lord do to the king of Assyria?

answers.text: Punish him for his arrogant heart
Reward him for a job well done

cards.text: Here's why: the king says, "By the strength of my hand I have done this, and by my wisdom, for I am clever." Friend, nobody clever has EVER said "for I am clever" out loud.

cards.question: True or false: The king of Assyria gives the LORD the credit for his victories.

cards.text: He keeps going: he's removed the boundaries of nations, plundered their treasures and subdued their rulers. He says it was like reaching into a nest and gathering abandoned eggs.

cards.question: The king says that as he gathered the earth, no wing fluttered and no beak opened or chirped. What's he bragging about?

answers.text: Nobody even tried to stop him
He struck while the world slept

cards.text: Then comes the answer to all that bragging, and it's a question: "Does an axe raise itself above the one who swings it?"

cards.question: In that picture, Assyria is the axe. So who's really doing the swinging?

cards.text: "Does a saw boast over him who saws with it?" Friend, I'm a stamper, and I never once stamped a cookie and turned around to Mother Miller like, "You're WELCOME," or I'd have landed in that drawer a whole lot sooner.
So the Lord GOD of Hosts will send a wasting disease among Assyria's stout warriors. And under all that pomp, a fire like a burning flame gets kindled.

cards.question: God is the Light of Israel and its Holy One. For Assyria, that Light will become a ___.

cards.text: The fire comes for Assyria's thorns and thistles. Then the splendor of its forests and orchards goes too, both soul and body, as a sickness consumes a man.

cards.question: True or false: The fire takes years to burn through Assyria's thorns and thistles.
When the fire is done, how many trees are left in Assyria's forests?

answers.text: So few a child could count them
Just enough to build one house
One left standing on each hill

findings.problem: Stop 1, card 1 quotes "Woe to Assyria.", which isn't the exact BSB wording.

rule.text: Quotes: Quotation marks around Bible words mean the exact BSB wording, punctuation included.

findings.problem: Stop 1, card 2 quotes "the rod of My anger.", which isn't the exact BSB wording.

rule.text: Quotes: Quotation marks around Bible words mean the exact BSB wording, punctuation included.

findings.problem: Card 5 has already told the baker that this is not Assyria's intention and not his plan. That rules out the wrong answer "To do only what God sends him for" before the question is asked, so only two answers are really in play.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: The joke compares Assyria's list of cities to "his to-do list." A to-do list holds tasks not done yet. Isaiah 10:10-11 has Assyria boasting about kingdoms he has already seized, Samaria included ("as I have done to Samaria"). The comparison doesn't match the core action of bragging about past conquests, and it suggests something the text shows is wrong.

rule.text: The everyday comparison must have the same action.

findings.problem: Card 8 only names the cities. It never tells the baker that Assyria pairs them as comparisons ("Is not Calno like Carchemish?... Is not Samaria like Damascus?"). Card 9 asks what point those comparisons make, but the baker was never given the comparisons to reason from.

rule.text: Before each choice card, Papa Dorin's story card gives enough context that the baker can reason their way to the answer.

findings.problem: Card 10, and then the card 11 question, name Jerusalem and Samaria together as the cities being measured against. Card 12 puts Samaria in the question, so Jerusalem is the only named place left. The wrong answers, Babylon and Egypt, appear nowhere in the lesson, so the earlier cards give the answer away.

rule.text: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later.

findings.problem: Card 3 quotes the king saying "By the strength of my hand I have done this, and by my wisdom." That gives away the answer to the card 4 true or false question about whether he gives the LORD the credit.

rule.text: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later.

findings.problem: Card 10 has just told the baker that "a fire like a burning flame gets kindled" against Assyria. The card 11 blank asks what the Light of Israel will become, and the answer is "fire," so the card right before it gives the answer away.

rule.text: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later.

findings.problem: Stop 2 opens with the same question-type pattern as stop 1: multiple choice, true or false, multiple choice. Multiple choice also dominates stop 2, with 4 multiple choice cards against 2 true or false and 1 fill in the blank.

rule.text: No stop repeats another stop's pattern, and no type dominates a stop by a wide margin.
